Competitive pressures and collective action problems together amplify AI risks by creating an environment where companies prioritize speed and market position over safety. Competitive pressures lead firms to reduce safety investments to keep up with rivals, resulting in a "race to the bottom" on safety standards. This dynamic encourages companies to release AI systems without adequate safety testing, increasing the likelihood of harmful outcomes.

Simultaneously, collective action problems prevent stakeholders from implementing safety measures that would benefit everyone. Even when there is agreement on the need for safety investments, individual actors may prefer to free-ride on the efforts of others, leading to systematic underinvestment in safety. This combination of competitive pressures and collective action problems results in a situation where AI risks are not only more likely to occur but also more severe, as the necessary safeguards are not put in place.
